meta.title: Local model
meta.description: Runs a llama.cpp model on this computer and offers it to the Harness as a selectable model provider. Open the Local model icon in the left sidebar. Status is live: the panel keeps one open stream from the Host and the Host samples once a second, so uptime, CPU and RAM usage, tokens processed, average time to first token, average tokens per second and the number of active calls update on their own — there is no refresh control, and a pill beside the title shows whether the stream is live, reconnecting or offline. The context window is reported honestly: this machine prefills roughly 100 to 250 tokens a second, so a stored value above the 32768 ceiling is reduced once to 8192 and the panel explains why, because the Harness keeps that much history before compacting and a larger window turns every answer into a minutes-long wait. The processed prompt state is also kept on disk, one file per model build, so a restart reuses the tokens it already read instead of re-reading them; a state written by another model is refused and discarded, because hidden states belong to the weights that produced them. Generation is capped, and the model's reasoning phase is off by default for a faster first token. Its Models card holds everything in one place, as a grid of icon controls: the models on this computer, four per page, each with a select control and a remove control, and a Hugging Face browser that stays empty until you search, twenty repositories per page. The folder control on a repository opens its GGUF builds below the grid with sizes, a Recommended tag on the Q4_K_M build, and a download control; split models download all their shards, downloads resume when interrupted, and gated repositories read HF_TOKEN from the environment that launches the Harness. You can also paste an org/repo, org/repo/file.gguf, or huggingface.co address. Install either published llama.cpp build first — CPU, or Vulkan for larger models that benefit from GPU offload; the Vulkan install sets GPU layers to 99. The panel also starts, stops, and restarts the server, and “Verify in Harness” sends one prompt through the same provider route the agent uses. To chat, open the model selector in the composer and pick the “Local model (llama.cpp)” group. The server keeps running while the panel is closed, and stops when you stop it or turn this plugin off. Prompts reach only the server on this machine; model files are read and written only under ~/.dsh/local-llm unless you point the paths elsewhere. A session whose tool schemas run to megabytes cannot fit a 1.7B local model; use it in a session with few tools. CPU and RAM describe the whole machine, and the token counters reset when the server restarts.
